sections.COMMENTS:
This Source is a NW-SE striking, SW-dipping normal fault on the western flank of the southern Apennines, toward the border with the central Apennines. It lies to the west of the well known, NE-dipping system of large normal fault that straddle the backbone of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a remarkable concentration of damaging and destructive earthquakes over the entire region and adjoining Composite Sources. The 9 September 1349, Lazio meridionale-Molise (Mw 6.6) is the one that has actually affected the area of this Source, but in fact other adjacent events cannot be ignored. The closest one is the 848, Sannio (Mw 6.0) event, although of uncertain location.
This Source is located in one of the most seismically active areas of peninsular Italy, in a region rich in destructive earthquakes, some of which of difficult explanation. This is certainly true for a very old earthquake like the 9 September 1349 one, which is in fact the southernmost sub-event of a multiple earthquake.
The main segment of this Source has been associated with the southern sub-event of the 1349 sequence. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on geological data from Galli and Naso (2009), like dip, and rake, the latter representing pure normal faulting. The minimum depth was based on geological data from Galli and Naso (2009), while maximum depth was calculated using the empirical relationships by Wells and Coppersmith (1994). The slip rate was deduced from the geological data from Galli and Naso (2009).
